trajectories, and retains workspaces through required live inspection.02The Experience Flywheel expands intents, environments, and verifiers
into executable tasks, then curates assessed trajectories.
The hard-task panel denotes skill-guided and checkpoint-assisted

policy for subsequent execution. GUI states, cursor cues, and rewards are
schematic. Trajectory rows omit intermediate actions, and GRPO retains valid
failures alongside successes.

Figure 3:Task scope and interaction.(a) Single-step grounding predicts a target location in a fixed screenshot.
The enlarged output view marks the zoom tool, with absolute pixel coordinates
in the original image.
(b) Desktop and web agents change software state through successive

Web observations also include DOM information.

header: 3NorthCUA Harness: Full-Lifecycle Infrastructure for Computer Use

images.caption:
Figure 4:NorthCUA Harness lifecycle.Within the expanded attempt, the shared runtime and long-horizon support
sustain GUI interaction while retaining the full trajectory. The evaluator
inspects recorded behavior and the live environment. Trajectory, task artifacts,
evaluation results, and task metadata are saved in an experience record before
the workspace is released. The lower lanes show parallel instances of this
lifecycle, coordinated by the batch collection service. GUI scenes, agent
imagery, and trajectories are illustrative.

Figure 5:Context for long-horizon execution.The complete trajectory is retained separately from the next-action context.
The visual window contains historical pre-action overlays and the latest clean
tool-result image. Textual action and result history can outlast image eviction
until compaction. Compaction summarizes earlier actions and results, omits old
GUI locators, and preserves recent complete exchanges and the current GUI.
An active agent-written note carries the overdue total from workbook to report.
PDF export remains unconfirmed. GUI scenes and the displayed visual-window size
are illustrative, with intermediate interactions omitted.

Figure 6:Action-aware visual feedback.Matched crops show the historical pre-action view with its NorthCUA overlay
(left) and the clean resulting state (right).01A click opens the chart dialog.02A drag moves a video clip earlier on its track.03Scrolling reveals route details below.04A text badge records the payload entered into the focused field.
Screenshots come from interactive GUI mockups with generated scenery.
Overlays use the unmodified runtime renderer. The input badge is enlarged
below its historical view.

Figure 7:Agentic outcome evaluation.Open questions guide selective retrieval and live inspection in the task
environment. E1 records an issued export, E2 establishes file presence, and
E3 exposes PDF contents for comparison with the source workbook. Unresolved
questions prompt further checks and can remain unresolved in the final report.
Evidence-linked findings distinguish task fulfillment from execution assessment.
GUI views, tool results, actions, and findings are illustrative. Generated
document views are cropped, intermediate actor actions are omitted, and
selected quality fields are shown without ratings.

Figure 8:Batch rollout at scale.(a) A centralized controller manages agent runners connected to device workers
in independent E2B sandboxes over long-lived WebSocket connections. Each worker
shares its sandbox’s lifecycle. (b) Staggered lifecycles overlap preparation,
execution, and evaluation. Ready intervals mark prepared environments awaiting
dispatch. Sandboxes remain available through live checks and output capture.
Record icons mark captured outputs that persist after release. The vertical
time slice marks concurrent stages. Timings and concurrency are schematic,
and GUI scenes are generated illustrations.

header: 4Experience Flywheel: Scaling Grounding and Agentic Experience

Figure 9:Constructing GUI grounding examples.(a) Screenshots cover public UI datasets, web-collected interfaces, and
states encountered in agent trajectories. (b) Visual annotations and available
accessibility metadata describe one target in its original screenshot.
(c) Name-, position-, and operation-based queries each form a separate
candidate example with the same clean screenshot and absolute target point.
The enlarged Day–Week–Month control group supplies the local evidence for
these descriptions. GUI assets are illustrative. Target outlines explain
construction, while training uses the unmarked1536×10241536\times 1024source image.

Figure 10:Documentation-guided control disambiguation.(a) The screenshot supplies the application, version, and located target.
(b) Online manual search retrieves control images and descriptions for visual
top-kkcandidates. One aligns the left edges of separate objects, while the
other aligns paragraph text within a fixed text object. (c) Panel and
selection context determine the function match, which guides query generation.
Each query retains the original screenshot and target point.
The GUI, documentation cards, and before/after operation diagrams are
illustrative. Documentation supports sample construction.

Figure 11:Three task-construction routes.Scaling Intents binds functions to file or website content before writing
requests. Scaling Environments prepares files and applications for sourced
requests or reconstructs website interfaces and backing state from references.
Scaling Verifiers jointly adapts requests, setup, and executable checks, then tests
tasks and verifiers. Each alternative route produces a complete task binding
a request, environment setup, and outcome assessment. GUI trials test completion
from the initial state, while result probes test acceptance of correct outcomes
and rejection of incorrect ones.
GUI assets and task packages are illustrative.

Figure 12:A concrete executable task contract.The saved commercial-review CaseSpec binds a request, input files, startup,
and output collection. The initial-workspace illustration redraws
representative source records in Calc. Requested deliverables comprise a
refreshable dashboard, an editable two-page memo with PDF export, and an
editable four-slide review deck. Inspection requirements summarize the
query, while post-run collection gathers available files for assessment.
GUI views, requested output layouts, abbreviated filenames, and the launch
command are illustrative.

Figure 13:Constructing a desktop base task.The selected Calc function narrows compatible workbooks.
Theorders.xlsxsummary grounds theStatus = Pendingcondition, while the persona guides request wording.
CaseSpec binds this request and file to startup instructions and the
required saved filter. The required view retains A17 and A58 and hides A42
without deleting source rows. Software and GUI assets, records, and setup
are illustrative. The right-hand view specifies a requirement, not an
observed rollout.

Figure 14:Constructing long-horizon tasks from blueprints.(1) Blueprint selection assembles work stages and prerequisites. Solid edges
carry content dependencies. The dashed C-to-D edge sets workflow order.
A node can require several GUI actions. (2) Materials bind the approved amount and
obsolete wording to inclusion and exclusion conditions for D’s PDF. C binds
an initial record to the required budget-decision update. (3) The grounded
plan guides LLM request writing and supplies the workspace and outcome
requirements in one CaseSpec. Its two outputs are the PDF and updated record.
Discovery facts remain in the prepared files. The structure follows a saved
plan. GUI details, the shortened request, and prospective outcomes are
illustrative.

Figure 15:Request-driven desktop environment construction.EnvAgent identifies the required resources, retrieves an order table, and
uses its identifiers to construct a missing shipment table. An LLM grounds
the sourced request in the prepared filenames and their shared Order ID
field. EnvAgent specifies startup and checks the materials and preparation
plan, revising inputs or instructions when checks fail before producing aCaseSpec.
The GUI agent subsequently performs the requested comparison.
GUI views and records are illustrative.

Figure 16:Reconstructing interactive websites from references.The aligned GUI views follow record R17 from the reference site to the local
implementation and a reload test. Observed pages and interactions guide the
interface and shared backing record. The test edits and saves the title, then
reloads the record to check persistence. Discrepancies return to implementation
for repair and retesting. The checked site is packaged with its declared initial
records and runtime configuration, separately from construction-test edits.
GUI states and URLs are illustrative.

Figure 17:Browser interaction guides iterative code repair.(1) The issue fixes the expected behavior. (2) The Coding Agent inspects and
edits the relevant implementation, then launches a candidate application.
(3) The Web Test Agent edits R17, saves the new title, and reloads the page.
The stacked views show the new title after saving and the old title after
reload, with cursor overlays marking interactions. A test report returns this
discrepancy, recorded actions, and screenshots to the Coding Agent for repair
and retesting under the unchanged expectation. Generated GUI views, code,
and test feedback are illustrative.

Figure 18:Bug-guided repair and targeted retesting.Desktop and narrow-screen tests produce one report, which guides both code
changes before retesting. Screenshots are later replays of archived code,
with subtitle line breaks cleaned for presentation. Overlays, report excerpts,
and abbreviated patches are explanatory. R2 passed three selected checks, including homepage
appearance, without repeating all five R1 items.

Figure 19:Expanding tasks and their verifiers together.The agent extracts a subtask, changes a selection criterion, or joins approval
with export, adapting completion and preservation checks to the new task.
The lower composition example separates a GUI execution trial from verifier
tests on prepared outcomes. The verdict column gives the requirement-derived
response for each probe. Testing checks whether the verifier returns it.
The task lists, generated GUI views, and hypothetical judgments illustrate
the construction procedure. The ellipsis omits intervening GUI actions, including
export. Initial-state preparation and repair iterations are not shown.

Figure 20:Accumulating operating knowledge through exploration.The source report contains “Quarterly,” but an image-only export makes
the phrase unsearchable in the PDF. Further exploration yields a
text-preserving procedure. An agent follows its fixed instructions in a
separate trial and searches the resulting PDF. The validated skill then
guides a new attempt in the original workspace, where full-task checks
determine trajectory acceptance. The return arrow depicts a failed task
attempt, while failed validation also prompts revision. Accepted trajectories retain the supplied skill
in context. GUI scenes, controls, actions, and outcomes are illustrative,
with intermediate exploratory trials omitted.

Figure 21:Retaining progress for branching trajectory search.Checkpoint M2 pairs the prepared report and software state with the agent
context. Independent continuations restore this checkpoint to try different
exports. The example contrasts image-only, text-preserving, and incomplete
single-page exports. The lower panel retains the common prefix and the chosen
continuation as one candidate path. The original task verifier checks the PDF,
earlier record update, and source preservation before accepting the trajectory.
Failed continuations leave the parent available for further attempts.
GUI states and diagnostic outcomes are illustrative.

Figure 22:Skill refinement in the TERRA dashboard case.Numbered annotations track chart orientation (1) and series colors (2)
through exploration, revised guidance, and a fresh attempt. Attempt 1
repairs the orientation during execution but fails the final palette check.
Attempt 2 applies skill v2 and passes all 26 final checks. Chart crops and
the final PDF come from recorded artifacts. Window frames and equivalent
Python excerpts are composed for presentation.

Figure 23:Milestone-guided construction of ORBIT BOTANICA.Three display milestones group the recorded checks. Teal frames mark one
retained path, and arrows preserve ancestry through omitted intermediate
steps. Branches can complete later work early. The equipped checkpoint and
its failed finishing continuation share the unchanged opaque-glass render.
Both successful finishing branches pass the full-task checks. Scene crops
are unretouched, with frames and diagnostic annotations added for presentation.

Figure 24:Joint desktop–web agentic reinforcement learning.The manager selects tasks, binds verifiers, and prepares isolated environments.
Workers use a model checkpoint to act through desktop or web interfaces.
Manager-run checks supply outcomes before workspace release. The adapter binds
outcomes to training samples while preserving each recorded input–response
pair and task/attempt identity. The learner uses GRPO to compare valid attempts
within the same task, initial-state, and verifier group, then returns an updated
checkpoint to workers. Worker and learner icons denote execution and training
uses of the same model. GUI scenes and binary outcomes are illustrative.
The example leaves task-group size unspecified.

Figure 25:Context-preserving RL sample construction.(a)The earlier input contains Overview and Editing. Appending the
typing result preserves history, so Enter title and Save share one segment.
After the successful Save action, Overview leaves the visual window (cross),
starting a new segment. The highlighted label marks the latest observation.
Gray objects supply context, while teal responses and token spans contribute
to policy loss.(b)Task-group outcomes determine one advantage per
attempt, shared across its segments. In the trajectory-mean configuration,
masked policy losses are pooled and normalized over each attempt’s target
tokens before averaging across attempts (Eq.1). Panel (a)
shows one continuous attempt under one behavior-policy version, with earlier
images unchanged until eviction. GUI states, responses, and outcomes are
illustrative. Thumbnails are input excerpts, strip lengths are schematic,
and earlier calls are omitted.

Figure 26:Grounding a documented control.Left, an actual documentation-grounded annotation pairs an Ample Bass P
control with its manual-defined articulation and a generated training query.
Right, NorthCUA localizes this control in an SSP screenshot with a different
surrounding GUI state, following the recorded querylegeto slide.
The target’s local appearance and position match the construction view.
In the enlarged detail, the teal box marks the reference target and the orange
point is the recorded prediction. Enlargements and annotations are reader aids. Documentation is
used in data construction, not supplied during direct evaluation.

Figure 27:Web success by website scope.The six groups partition all 812 WebArena-Verified tasks using retained
attempts. Nano and Mini use SFT checkpoints, while Pro uses RL.
Pro exceeds 70% in every single-site group and completes 17 of 48
cross-site tasks. AppendixIgives the
selection and group details.

Figure 28:Source-paper selection before and after long-horizon SFT.
A shared question anchors the two equal-width result views. Agent callouts
paraphrase recorded selection and checking decisions. Highlighted filenames
show the different Q3 sources, while scores cover each complete attempt.
Screenshots are cropped observations before the indexed decisions, with
enlarged filenames.
The runs use different dataset revisions and OCR settings.

Figure 30:Executed trajectories with contrasting task rewards.Both Thunderbird attempts reach Tags view. A hides the entire header,
while B disables Get Messages specifically. Native screenshot crops show
executed click positions in the middle panels and the state before
application closure on the right. A’s first two panels crop one observation.
B opens the header menu between those panels. The archived configuration verifier
returns rewards 0 and 1. Both attempts belong to one eight-member GRPO
group containing five successes and three failures, which determines
their advantage signs. They span an asynchronous policy update.
This is a within-group reward comparison, not a before/after checkpoint
evaluation.

Figure 31:Recovering from an unavailable browser action.In a retained Pro evaluation attempt, NorthCUA first attempts to select
an unavailable Quarter period. It inspects the dropdown, switches to Month
with the exact Q1 date range, and reads the resulting table before answering
Sprite. The saved evaluator marks the task successful. Numbered panels
show observations before decisions 6, 10, and 12 of a 13-decision attempt,
with intermediate actions omitted. Detail views enlarge original control
crops, with field labels arranged for readability. The answer at decision 13
and the external evaluator’s success marker are annotations outside the webpage.

Figure 32:Choice-based Web execution.The input shows the title before editing. Generated GUI views illustrate
filling the new title (right) and a subsequent Save click (left).
At each decision, current controls support operation and target selection.
A direct choice executes without decoding, while a generation route triggers
a second full-model call with the original prompt and a fresh cache.
Optional LoRA adapters are active only for classification.
Route and target checks are omitted.

Figure 33:Ultrafast product-update case.Selected Head + LoRA decisions from one WebArena-Verified attempt.
Lightning and text-entry icons distinguish direct choice from native
generation. Numbers retain the original decision indices, with intermediate
steps omitted. Insets enlarge recorded details, with post-action states labeled.

Figure 34:Four states of the same report task.Missing output and missing regional detail should be rejected.
A complete table and an equivalent chart should be accepted.

regional discussion, template compliance, and unchanged source files.
The GUI excerpts and inspection asset are illustrative.
The dashed red region annotates missing content.
Accept/Reject labels show the expected verdicts for these illustrative states.
